{
  "draft_contract_sha256_acknowledged": "c279c328018c9e37e2d2676adc9f0c5118886a1a3e9222a2206ff99b723bdb35",
  "verdict": "PASS_TO_SEPARATELY_AUTHORIZED_E1_B_TRANSITION_RUNTIME_PILOT",
  "historical_update_selection_assessment": "The contract binds exactly eight historical E0 pool_k8.json artifacts by absolute path, task_id, and SHA-256 under the same e0_root used by the prior provider-runtime Pilot, and the runner revalidates each file SHA and task binding in the declared order through load_selected_pools. The declared selection rule is lexicographic and frozen before reading mixed/rescue/outcome fields for this Pilot; the code does not reselect pools after observing any learned-skill or development outcome. The update stream is ProjectionName.WINNER_ONLY only. The V3.1 path uses ExactMatchedEvidenceBlockRenderer, BlindedEvidenceUnit, arm-blinded evidence text, and selected-evidence-trajectory score semantics; no MRW stream is constructed in the transition runner.",
  "development_task_selection_assessment": "The development task is fixed in the draft contract as r17-b0-agj-p4, and the bound split manifest shows r17-b0-agj-p4 is the lexicographically first development task. The contract states the task is frozen before learned-skill outcome observation and is not used for scientific effectiveness. The transition runner passes exactly that task ID to the actor and later requires the actor summary task list to equal that single task. The authorization validator requires allowed_task_ids to equal exactly that task. No code path reads e1_common_heldout_probe or selects the task based on performance.",
  "updater_causal_purity_assessment": "The updater path remains the V3.1 causally pure path. The transition runner reuses evidence_units from the provider-runtime helper, which instantiates ExactMatchedEvidenceBlockRenderer, renders exact re-tokenized parity blocks, rejects forbidden visible provenance markers, and constructs BlindedEvidenceUnit objects. run_projection_update receives blinded_evidence_units, places only unit.evidence_text in model-visible messages, and sets score to unit.source_score. The dedicated updater runtime is independently qualified, the transition runner must itself execute under that runtime, MindMemOS is pinned to commit 90491828726e1540442b17cd445d0308d0b8093c with a clean checkout, and the updater uses temperature 0.0 by adapter default, provider_retry_limit 0, thinking disabled, and max_parse_attempts 1. No MRW or A/B comparison is executed.",
  "noninitial_skill_receipt_handoff_assessment": "After the WIN update, the actor receives --skill-source pointing to update/win/skill_post and --updater-receipt pointing to update/win/update_receipt.json. The actor runner resolves skill_post/SKILL.md, computes its SHA, and because the source differs from the default initial skill, requires E1 mode plus a completed updater receipt. It validates that the receipt binds the exact resolved skill path, exact skill content SHA, the same contract SHA as the authorization, and the same authorization SHA. The transition runner additionally requires the actor summary to report the learned skill SHA and updater receipt SHA. Omitting a pre-known learned-skill SHA from authorization scope is scientifically acceptable here because the learned SHA is only defined after the provider update; the authorization instead explicitly allows noninitial skill loading and the receipt content-addresses the learned artifact after the fact.",
  "actor_runtime_and_verifier_assessment": "Actor execution is launched with the independently frozen actor/evaluator venv python after validate_actor_runtime checks the venv, freeze SHA, qualification SHA, and import smoke. The actor runner uses the same controlled suite root, SpreadsheetBenchEnv, ReactAgentFactory, exact DeepSeek requested/resolved identity from the fresh model-identity adjudication, K=1, max_turns=10, max_output_tokens=4096, concurrency=1, temperature=0, thinking disabled, and provider_retry_limit=0. The transition runner validates that the actor summary loaded the learned skill SHA, bound updater receipt SHA, K=1, and exactly the fixed development task. It records the evaluation summary SHA but does not promote or interpret the task score.",
  "shared_provider_budget_assessment": "One SQLite ProviderBudgetLedger at checkpoints/provider_budget.sqlite3 is shared by the updater subprocess path and actor subprocess. It is bound to the exact contract SHA and authorization SHA, with total_limit 20 and per_unit_limit 10. Claims are committed before provider I/O and never released. The updater uses unit e1-b-transition/update_win and is required to consume exactly 10 calls; the actor rollout uses unit r17-b0-agj-p4/rollout_0 and can claim at most 10 calls, with the global 20-call cap also enforced. Neither role can reset or reinitialize an existing ledger because resume opens with allow_create false and metadata drift fails closed.",
  "checkpoint_failure_preservation_assessment": "A completed update may be safely reused: checkpoints/update_completed.json content-addresses the update receipt and skill_post, and the runner revalidates both SHAs before evaluation. If update artifacts exist without a completed checkpoint, or evaluation artifacts exist without a completed summary, the runner refuses automatic rerun. On actor failure it writes checkpoints/evaluation_failure.json with provider_relaunch_authorized false and raises while preserving the stale lock. The lock is deleted only after full success. This is consistent with the failure-differential policy: partial or ambiguous provider-facing state is preserved and diagnosed rather than silently rerun.",
  "scientific_boundary_assessment": "The Pilot maintains the required boundary: e1_common_heldout_accessed is false, no held-out task IDs are passed to the actor, no WIN-A/WIN-B equivalence inference is performed, no MRW stream or causal comparison is executed, no learned-skill effect is promoted, and paper/frontend/submission authority is false. The single development outcome is used only to prove that the frozen actor/evaluator completes with a receipt-bound noninitial skill.",
  "failure_learning_policy_assessment": "The contract and runner appropriately separate runtime/implementation failure from scientific-mechanism failure. A transition failure is preserved as technical state with stale lock and no automatic relaunch; it cannot be interpreted against R17's mechanism because this Pilot reaches no scientific endpoint. Conversely, a PASS only establishes the update-to-noninitial-skill evaluation handoff and verifier completion; it does not support the R17 mechanism, MRW benefit, or E1-B scientific claims.",
  "remaining_blockers": [],
  "nonblocking_notes": [
    "The transition runner requires the updater to consume exactly 10 provider calls, matching the observed nominal first-party SkillEvolver call structure from the prior provider-runtime Pilot; this is appropriate for this frozen runtime handoff but means any future first-party updater call-structure change must be handled by a new versioned contract rather than local relaxation.",
    "The actor authorization requires scientific_experiment=true because the shared actor runner uses that bit for bound E1 actor execution, while the transition contract itself remains non-scientific in interpretation; the additional authority bits e1_b_negative_control=false, mrw_causal_comparison=false, paper_promotion=false, exact task scope, K=1, and receipt binding prevent scientific expansion.",
    "The development task score is recorded only inside the actor/evaluation artifacts and is explicitly not used for promotion, selection, or effectiveness claims."
  ],
  "transition_runtime_pilot_recommendation": "ALLOW_SEPARATE_FROZEN_TRANSITION_RUNTIME_PILOT_AUTHORIZATION",
  "e1_b_negative_control_recommendation": "HOLD",
  "mrw_causal_comparison_recommendation": "HOLD",
  "paper_claim_authority": false,
  "single_sentence_verdict": "PASS: the draft transition Pilot is a narrowly scoped, receipt-bound runtime handoff from one WIN-only historical update to one fixed K=1 development evaluation, with no E1 held-out access, MRW execution, scientific effectiveness inference, or paper authority."
}

review.actor_runtime_and_verifier_assessment: Actor execution is launched with the independently frozen actor/evaluator venv python after validate_actor_runtime checks the venv, freeze SHA, qualification SHA, and import smoke. The actor runner uses the same controlled suite root, SpreadsheetBenchEnv, ReactAgentFactory, exact DeepSeek requested/resolved identity from the fresh model-identity adjudication, K=1, max_turns=10, max_output_tokens=4096, concurrency=1, temperature=0, thinking disabled, and provider_retry_limit=0. The transition runner validates that the actor summary loaded the learned skill SHA, bound updater receipt SHA, K=1, and exactly the fixed development task. It records the evaluation summary SHA but does not promote or interpret the task score.
review.checkpoint_failure_preservation_assessme: A completed update may be safely reused: checkpoints/update_completed.json content-addresses the update receipt and skill_post, and the runner revalidates both SHAs before evaluation. If update artifacts exist without a completed checkpoint, or evaluation artifacts exist without a completed summary, the runner refuses automatic rerun. On actor failure it writes checkpoints/evaluation_failure.json with provider_relaunch_authorized false and raises while preserving the stale lock. The lock is deleted only after full success. This is consistent with the failure-differential policy: partial or ambiguous provider-facing state is preserved and diagnosed rather than silently rerun.
review.development_task_selection_assessment: The development task is fixed in the draft contract as r17-b0-agj-p4, and the bound split manifest shows r17-b0-agj-p4 is the lexicographically first development task. The contract states the task is frozen before learned-skill outcome observation and is not used for scientific effectiveness. The transition runner passes exactly that task ID to the actor and later requires the actor summary task list to equal that single task. The authorization validator requires allowed_task_ids to equal exactly that task. No code path reads e1_common_heldout_probe or selects the task based on performance.
review.failure_learning_policy_assessment: The contract and runner appropriately separate runtime/implementation failure from scientific-mechanism failure. A transition failure is preserved as technical state with stale lock and no automatic relaunch; it cannot be interpreted against R17's mechanism because this Pilot reaches no scientific endpoint. Conversely, a PASS only establishes the update-to-noninitial-skill evaluation handoff and verifier completion; it does not support the R17 mechanism, MRW benefit, or E1-B scientific claims.
review.historical_update_selection_assessment: The contract binds exactly eight historical E0 pool_k8.json artifacts by absolute path, task_id, and SHA-256 under the same e0_root used by the prior provider-runtime Pilot, and the runner revalidates each file SHA and task binding in the declared order through load_selected_pools. The declared selection rule is lexicographic and frozen before reading mixed/rescue/outcome fields for this Pilot; the code does not reselect pools after observing any learned-skill or development outcome. The update stream is ProjectionName.WINNER_ONLY only. The V3.1 path uses ExactMatchedEvidenceBlockRenderer, BlindedEvidenceUnit, arm-blinded evidence text, and selected-evidence-trajectory score semantics; no MRW stream is constructed in the transition runner.
nonblocking_notes: The transition runner requires the updater to consume exactly 10 provider calls, matching the observed nominal first-party SkillEvolver call structure from the prior provider-runtime Pilot; this is appropriate for this frozen runtime handoff but means any future first-party updater call-structure change must be handled by a new versioned contract rather than local relaxation.

The actor authorization requires scientific_experiment=true because the shared actor runner uses that bit for bound E1 actor execution, while the transition contract itself remains non-scientific in interpretation; the additional authority bits e1_b_negative_control=false, mrw_causal_comparison=false, paper_promotion=false, exact task scope, K=1, and receipt binding prevent scientific expansion.
The development task score is recorded only inside the actor/evaluation artifacts and is explicitly not used for promotion, selection, or effectiveness claims.
review.noninitial_skill_receipt_handoff_assessm: After the WIN update, the actor receives --skill-source pointing to update/win/skill_post and --updater-receipt pointing to update/win/update_receipt.json. The actor runner resolves skill_post/SKILL.md, computes its SHA, and because the source differs from the default initial skill, requires E1 mode plus a completed updater receipt. It validates that the receipt binds the exact resolved skill path, exact skill content SHA, the same contract SHA as the authorization, and the same authorization SHA. The transition runner additionally requires the actor summary to report the learned skill SHA and updater receipt SHA. Omitting a pre-known learned-skill SHA from authorization scope is scientifically acceptable here because the learned SHA is only defined after the provider update; the authorization instead explicitly allows noninitial skill loading and the receipt content-addresses the learned artifact after the fact.
review.scientific_boundary_assessment: The Pilot maintains the required boundary: e1_common_heldout_accessed is false, no held-out task IDs are passed to the actor, no WIN-A/WIN-B equivalence inference is performed, no MRW stream or causal comparison is executed, no learned-skill effect is promoted, and paper/frontend/submission authority is false. The single development outcome is used only to prove that the frozen actor/evaluator completes with a receipt-bound noninitial skill.
review.shared_provider_budget_assessment: One SQLite ProviderBudgetLedger at checkpoints/provider_budget.sqlite3 is shared by the updater subprocess path and actor subprocess. It is bound to the exact contract SHA and authorization SHA, with total_limit 20 and per_unit_limit 10. Claims are committed before provider I/O and never released. The updater uses unit e1-b-transition/update_win and is required to consume exactly 10 calls; the actor rollout uses unit r17-b0-agj-p4/rollout_0 and can claim at most 10 calls, with the global 20-call cap also enforced. Neither role can reset or reinitialize an existing ledger because resume opens with allow_create false and metadata drift fails closed.
review.single_sentence_verdict: PASS: the draft transition Pilot is a narrowly scoped, receipt-bound runtime handoff from one WIN-only historical update to one fixed K=1 development evaluation, with no E1 held-out access, MRW execution, scientific effectiveness inference, or paper authority.
review.updater_causal_purity_assessment: The updater path remains the V3.1 causally pure path. The transition runner reuses evidence_units from the provider-runtime helper, which instantiates ExactMatchedEvidenceBlockRenderer, renders exact re-tokenized parity blocks, rejects forbidden visible provenance markers, and constructs BlindedEvidenceUnit objects. run_projection_update receives blinded_evidence_units, places only unit.evidence_text in model-visible messages, and sets score to unit.source_score. The dedicated updater runtime is independently qualified, the transition runner must itself execute under that runtime, MindMemOS is pinned to commit 90491828726e1540442b17cd445d0308d0b8093c with a clean checkout, and the updater uses temperature 0.0 by adapter default, provider_retry_limit 0, thinking disabled, and max_parse_attempts 1. No MRW or A/B comparison is executed.
